title: Hardwood Floors in a New Build vs a Remodel: What Changes in Lynnwood
meta: Hardwood floors in a Lynnwood new build vs a remodel: same $3.25 per sq ft labor, very different sequencing, subfloor and moisture. Wills Flooring explains.
keywords: hardwood floors new construction vs remodel, hardwood installation Lynnwood WA, builder flooring allowance hardwood, when to install hardwood in new build, hardwood floors remodel old house
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: The installation labor is identical, $3.25 per sq ft for prefinished and $2.75 for unfinished, but almost everything around the floor changes: sequencing, subfloor, moisture, trim and who else is on site.
blocks.detail: In a Lynnwood new build the floor waits on six other trades. In a 1970s Alderwood remodel it waits on whatever we find under the carpet.

blocks.html: Lynnwood is building fast around the light rail station, and at the same time a generation of Alderwood, Meadowdale and Martha Lake ramblers and split-levels is being opened up and remodeled. We install hardwood in both, sometimes in the same week, and the questions are completely different. New-build buyers ask whether to take the builder's flooring allowance. Remodelers ask what happens when the carpet comes up. Here is what actually changes, and what doesn't. Our full rate card is on the hardwood installation page.

blocks.text: What stays the same: the labor rates

items.title: Prefinished engineered or solid
items.text: Nail-down, glue-down or floating, factory-finished planks. Walk on it the day we finish. Same rate whether the house is two months old or fifty years old.

items.title: Unfinished, site-finished
items.text: Raw planks installed, then sanded and finished in place at our refinishing rates. Flat, seamless, and you pick the exact stain. Needs an empty house.

items.title: Hardwood on stairs
items.text: Treads, risers and nosings on a split-level or townhome staircase, priced per stair on top of the floor area.

blocks.note: Labor only, 500 sq ft minimum. Material, underlayment, old-floor removal and subfloor prep are quoted at the free estimate.

blocks.text: How the schedule runs in each project

items.text: We visit once the house is closed in and the heat is running. Moisture readings decide the delivery date, not the GC's wish list.
items.note: Subfloor and wood within 2 to 4 points of each other

items.text: Wood acclimates on site three to five days at living temperature. Then we install, roughly 400 to 600 sq ft per day.
items.note: A 1,400 sq ft townhome main level runs 3 days

items.text: Painters finish, trim carpenter sets base and shoe, doors are hung. For a site-finished floor we return to sand and finish after paint.
We pull back a carpet corner in a closet. Many Alderwood and Martha Lake homes have oak already there; others have plank subfloor that needs a plywood layer.
items.note: If there is oak, refinishing may beat new hardwood

items.text: Carpet, pad and tack strip out. Staples pulled, squeaks screwed down, humps sanded, dips filled. Wood delivered and stacked in the rooms.
Install room by room so you keep a path through the house. Base back on or shoe added, transitions set, doors undercut.

blocks.text: Prefinished or unfinished? The answer flips

a.title: Usually wins in a remodel
items: You are living in the house and need to walk on it tonight
No finish smell, no 72-hour cure, no dust from sanding
Rooms can be done one at a time around furniture
Factory aluminum-oxide finish is harder than anything applied on site

b.title: Usually wins in a new build
items: House is empty, so sanding dust and cure time cost nothing
Perfectly flat floor with no beveled edges between boards
You choose the exact stain and sheen after seeing it on your wood
Stairs, landings and floor finish all match because they were finished together

blocks.title: About the builder's flooring allowance:
blocks.text: Ask what the allowance actually buys and what the credit is if you decline it. In a lot of Lynnwood new construction the standard option is a thin-wear-layer engineered plank, and the credit for skipping it is smaller than its retail value. Your own installer after closing often gets a better floor for similar money, but only if the builder leaves the subfloor bare and holds the base trim. Get that in writing.
Mistakes that cost money in each kind of project

items.html: New build: installing on a wet subfloor. Fresh OSB at 16 percent will shrink and leave gaps by the first winter. We wait for numbers, not dates.
New build: floor in before the painters are done. Ladders, drips and dust on a new floor. Floor goes in after primer and before final coats.
Remodel: skipping the subfloor look. A quote that never lifted the carpet is a guess. Plank subfloors in 1960s ramblers usually need a plywood overlay before nail-down hardwood.
Remodel: not checking for oak first. Plenty of Lynnwood carpets hide sound red oak. Refinishing at $3.99 per sq ft can beat new hardwood at $3.25 plus material.
Both: forgetting transitions and door clearance. New hardwood sits higher than carpet. Doors need undercutting and tile thresholds need a real transition.

blocks.text: Your checklist before you sign either contract

items.html: New build: written confirmation that the subfloor stays bare, base trim stays off, and HVAC runs two weeks before delivery.
Remodel: a quote written after someone actually looked under the carpet, with removal, subfloor prep and trim as separate lines.
Both: a moisture reading on the subfloor recorded on the quote, and an acclimation plan for the wood.
Both: a decision on prefinished vs site-finished made on your schedule, not the installer's convenience.
Both: licensed, insured, and a written workmanship warranty. Ours is one year, from Lynnwood since 2013.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to install hardwood in a new build or a remodel?
faq.a: The labor rate is the same, $3.25 per sq ft prefinished and $2.75 unfinished. A new build is usually cheaper overall because there is no old floor to remove, no trim to pull and the subfloor is new. A remodel adds removal and prep lines priced at the estimate.

faq.q: Should I take the builder's flooring allowance or hire my own installer?
faq.a: Compare the actual product in the allowance with the credit for declining it. If the credit is fair and the builder will leave the subfloor bare and trim off, your own installer after closing usually gets a better floor. If the credit is small, the allowance can still win.

faq.q: When in the construction schedule should hardwood go in?
faq.a: After drywall and primer, once HVAC has run about two weeks and the subfloor reads dry, and before final paint, base trim and interior doors. We prefer to run the floor under cabinets so a future kitchen change is not locked in.

faq.q: Can you match new hardwood to the existing oak in my split-level?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Lynnwood split-levels almost always have 2 1/4 inch red oak strip. We source the same species and width, then refinish everything together for a seamless match or set a flush transition where the floors meet.

faq.q: How long does hardwood need to acclimate in a new house?
faq.a: Three to five days in the rooms where it will go, with heat at normal living temperature. The real test is the meter: wood and subfloor within a few percentage points. New construction often needs longer because the framing is still drying.

faq.q: Do you remove the old carpet in a remodel?
faq.a: Yes. Carpet, pad, tack strip and staples come out and we haul them away, as a separate line on the written quote so you can compare it with doing it yourself. We screw down squeaks and fix the subfloor before any wood goes down.
